name: Impacket - DCSync with Kerberos Ticket
description: Performs a DCSync using a Kerberos ticket (-k -no-pass, with KRB5CCNAME set) to replicate a target account's hashes from the DC. With a machine-account TGT (for example DC01$) this dumps the Administrator or krbtgt hash.
notes:
DCSync (`secretsdump -just-dc` / mimikatz lsadump::dcsync) impersonates a DC's replication to pull ANY account's hash - including krbtgt for golden tickets. Needs Replicating Directory Changes rights (Domain Admin or delegated).
Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 19 (Password Attacks)

recommended.note: Full NTDS dump for all hashes.
Crack the dumped NT hashes after DCSync.

defense.why_it_works: Using a certificate/TGT obtained for a DC or privileged account (via ADCS abuse), the attacker performs DCSync to replicate password hashes.
defense.prerequisites: A TGT/cert for an account with replication rights (or a DC identity).
defense.impact: Domain password hashes (incl. krbtgt) via DCSync - full domain compromise.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1003.006] Event 4662 with the replication GUIDs from a non-DC principal; the preceding certificate/PKINIT logon.
defense.artifacts: 4662 replication events; the certificate-based logon that enabled it.
defense.prevention: [MITRE T1003.006] restrict replication rights and DC identities; RPC firewall for replication; harden ADCS so DC certs can't be forged; monitor 4662.
defense.evasion: The certificate path avoids touching LSASS/credentials on hosts; DCSync from a DC-identity looks like replication.
defense.misconfiguration: Pass-the-Certificate (PtC) attacks exploit ADCS certificate abuse (ESC1/ESC8) combined with Kerberos PKINIT. Shadow credentials (pywhisker) exploit write access to msDS-KeyCredentialLink to add a certificate-based authentication mechanism to any account. Pass-the-Ticket works because Kerberos tickets are extractable from LSASS memory.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# msDS-KeyCredentialLink writable by attacker (GenericWrite on target account):
# pywhisker.py -t targetuser -a add
# Adds a fake device credential -> obtain certificate for targetuser
# -> PKINIT TGT as targetuser -> NTLM hash via UnPAC

# LSASS memory contains TGTs for all logged-in users:
# Mimikatz: sekurlsa::tickets /export
# Rubeus: dump /all
defense.secure_config:
# Prevent msDS-KeyCredentialLink abuse:
# Audit who has GenericWrite on privileged accounts
# Only SYSTEM/DCs should write msDS-KeyCredentialLink
Get-ObjectAcl -Identity admin -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object {$_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'Write'}

# Prevent ticket extraction:
# Enable Credential Guard (blocks LSASS memory reads)
# Protected Users group members: tickets not cached in LSASS

# ADCS: prevent ESC1/ESC8 (see those cards)
# Monitor: Event 4768 with certificate auth, Event 4769 unusual ticket lifetimes
